A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self is a space of tension in which different and even opposite forces are in constant interaction, resulting in the continuous emergence of new positions.
the self is pulled by two mutually complementary movements: decentering and centering.
the space of the modern self is being stretched in opposite directions, leading to a tension that is felt as a crisis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self is not only a center that holds but also a space that is extended in a variety of different directions, and that, instead of being held together, it is pulled apart.
the self has become increasingly vulnerable to forces of fragmentation, disintegration, or even dissolution as the center of the self is no longer able to hold.
the self is not a single, unified, and coherent entity, but a multiplicity of relatively autonomous I-positions that simultaneously function as a minisocial system.
